answer: A triple re-execution check stops a sybil farm from scaling. Every submitted task is rerun by two independent verifiers, and all three results must match before any reward is released. One honest agent passes easily, but a farm of a thousand identities must pay for a thousand matching reruns, each costing real compute and time, so its cost grows in lockstep with its size. A lantern burning through the night marks the honest worker still present at dawn, while a dune of fakes collapses because every grain must be rechecked, and the horizon of profit shrinks with each added clone.
